newsitem.title: USA: Nationwide to reduce sales in coastal areas.
newsitem.headline: Nationwide to reduce sales in coastal areas.

text.p: Nationwide Insurance said it will reduce the sales of new property insurance policies in the coastal counties of 17 states, from Maine to Texas.
Nationwide said the changes won't affect existing customers, except possibly a small number with property on barrier islands or very close to coastlines.
Nationwide said the move will not actually halt sales in Florida, but will mean no sales growth as it simply replaces business as it expires on a one-for-one basis.
In other coastal regions, Nationwide said it will slow the pace of sales growth, but not stop it.

"This is an additional move by the company in its constant effort to manage growth in areas that are highly vulnerable to extraordinary property losses from severe windstorms and hurricanes," Richard Crabtree, president of Nationwide property-casualty companies, said in a statement.

"We've been limiting our growth of new policies in coastal areas for some time," he said, "but losses we've sustained in Huricane Fran reinforce the need for Nationwide to further limit growth of new property coverages in coastal areas."
The modified growth program is being implemented immediately on a state-by-state basis, Nationwide said.
Programs will be tailored specifically to satisfy circumstances in each state, the company said.
Nationwide said it will work closely with state insurance departments to obtain any needed statutory approvals.
The company said planning for the modified growth program was begun nine months ago.
Nationwide said it periodically reviews its exposures to natural disasters.
"As we learn more about extraordinary losses that the company might sustain, we may need to take appropriate action in the future," Crabtree said.

Nationwide has a policyholder surplus of more than $5 billion tha provides the company with a very strong safety net to deal with catastrophic losses, Nationwide chief financial officer Robert Oakley said.
Nationwide also has significant catastrophic reinsurance protection and has immediate access to additional capital through its recent contingent surplus note offering.
"Nationwide Insurance possesses great financial strength -- and we intend to keep it that way," Oakley said.
"We owe it to our policyholders to protect Nationwide's financial resources, and this is an effective way to accomplish that goal," Oakley said.
Nationwide has 2.6 million homeowners policies in force, an increase of nearly 800,000 since 1990. The company's commercial policies total nearly 801,000, up 309,000 in the past five years.
